Link-refresh-only PR. I verified each target live:

- `https://ubuntu.com/enterprise-store/docs/` — 200 (markdown). Note the previous `documentation.ubuntu.com/enterprise-store` already 301s here, so this is forward-looking cleanup, not a fix of a broken link.
- `https://docs.cloud-init.io/` — 200 (redirects to `/en/latest/`).
- `https://canonical.com/maas` and `https://canonical.com/multipass` — 200.
- `https://wiki.ubuntu.com/IptablesHowTo` — **HTTP 404**. The legacy MoinMoin content was retired when the new Ubuntu Wiki (MediaWiki) launched, and `help.ubuntu.com/community/IptablesHowTo` just redirects to this same 404. So `logging.md` is left broken; see the inline note for a verified replacement.
- `/how-to-guides/manage-machines.md` (deploy-dpus.md) — valid: target exists and root-relative `.md` links are the established convention in this docs tree (e.g. `decommission-maas.md:27`, `how-to-guides/index.md:20-34`). `docs/conf.py` `linkcheck_ignore` does not cover `wiki.ubuntu.com`, so the `make -C docs linkcheck` pre-commit hook (docs/.sphinx/.pre-commit-config.yaml:11) would fail on the 404.

No security or correctness concerns beyond the broken link; the remaining edits are cosmetic and safe.

docs/reference/configuration-guides/logg.16: This URL is dead: `https://wiki.ubuntu.com/IptablesHowTo` returns HTTP 404 (verified), and the old `https://help.ubuntu.com/community/IptablesHowTo` now redirects to that same 404, so the change does not actually fix the reference. Use a live target instead, e.g. `https://documentation.ubuntu.com/server/how-to/security/firewalls/` (verified 200; it documents both iptables and ufw and the firewall log setup this section discusses). Note `make -C docs linkcheck` is a pre-commit hook here and `linkcheck_ignore` in docs/conf.py does not exempt `wiki.ubuntu.com`, so a 404 will be flagged.

docs/how-to-guides/set-up-air-gapped-maa.20: New target verified 200, but the old link already 301'd here, so nothing was broken. Two nits while you are in this section: step 2 above (line 18) says "Secure your deployment with HTTP" — for a store serving snaps to restricted networks this should read HTTPS; and linking the docs landing page is fine, but `https://ubuntu.com/enterprise-store/docs/how-to` is closer to the offline/air-gapped procedure being described.

docs/how-to-guides/deploy-dpus.md.425: Internal target is correct (`docs/how-to-guides/manage-machines.md` exists and root-relative `.md` links match the tree's convention). Minor: the escaped hyphen in `\-` is no longer needed for a plain link label, and this line dropped the trailing double-space hard break that lines 426-427 still carry — harmless in a list but inconsistent.
